items.stem: A company needs consistent, private, high-bandwidth connectivity between its data centre and AWS, independent of the public internet. Which option best meets this?

options.text: A dedicated private network connection (Direct Connect-style)
options.rationale: Correct: a dedicated private connection provides consistent, private, high-bandwidth connectivity independent of the internet.

options.text: A site-to-site VPN over the public internet only
options.rationale: A VPN over the internet cannot guarantee consistent bandwidth or avoid the public path.
This is object access, not private network connectivity.

items.explanation: Correct: a dedicated private connection provides consistent, private, high-bandwidth connectivity independent of the internet.

items.stem: Two VPCs that must be connected were created with identical, overlapping CIDR ranges. What is the core problem for simple VPC peering?

options.text: Overlapping CIDRs create ambiguous routing, so standard peering cannot route between them
options.rationale: Correct: overlapping address ranges make routing ambiguous and break simple peering.

options.text: CIDR ranges are irrelevant to peering
options.rationale: Addressing is central to peering feasibility.

items.explanation: Correct: overlapping address ranges make routing ambiguous and break simple peering.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about AWS security groups versus network ACLs are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Security groups are stateful; return traffic is automatically allowed
Network ACLs are stateless and evaluate rules in order with explicit allow/deny
options.rationale: Correct: NACLs are stateless and process numbered rules.

options.text: Security groups can explicitly deny specific traffic
options.rationale: Security groups only allow; they cannot explicitly deny.

options.text: Network ACLs are stateful like security groups
options.rationale: NACLs are stateless, unlike security groups.

options.text: Both operate only at the DNS layer
options.rationale: Neither operates at the DNS layer.

items.explanation: Correct: security groups are stateful. Correct: NACLs are stateless and process numbered rules.
